done.why: I got the jewelled egg into the trophy case by turn 45, and the case listed it as my collection. After that I went underground, killed the troll, got through the Loud Room and took the platinum bar. The trap door had been barred behind me and the rest of the world is huge, so once my own goal was done I stopped at 60 points.

about: It's the white house in the woods with a trophy case "that expects to be filled". Treasure is scattered through the forest and the caves below, and the game keeps quietly pointing out how fragile some of it is and who might want it, like the egg's clasp needing "not entirely honest" fingers.

ending.what: The jewel-encrusted egg is in the trophy case, unopened and unbroken. The case and the room description both show 'Your collection of treasures consists of: A jewel-encrusted egg.' My score was 20, and 60 later.

moments.note: The trophy case has 'the patient air of something that expects to be filled'. A lovely nudge toward the goal.
The nest's description: a songbird 'with better taste in treasure than in architecture'.
The egg's clasp needs 'deft fingers, and not entirely honest ones'. A clear hint not to force it myself.
I could carry the fragile egg inside the nest. It felt like the careful thing to do, and the game let me.
The egg went into the case cleanly and the room now lists my collection.
The trap door crashed shut and someone barred it behind me.
The troll died to my very first sword blow, which was surprisingly easy.
Couldn't take the axe: 'Your load is too heavy, the sword not least of it.' Fair, but abrupt.
In the Loud Room every command just echoed back ('Score score ...', 'North north ...'). It took me a while to realise the room was eating my words.
Saying 'echo' changed the acoustics, and the platinum bar became takeable.

wished: Open the egg myself, or at least try to without being told off, to see what's inside
Get back up through the barred trap door, or find another way out of the cellar, to bring the platinum bar home to the case
Have some sign, when the egg went in, that the case had been waiting for it, beyond a plain 'Done.'

lines.line: It has the patient air of something that expects to be filled.
lines.why: It set up the whole goal with one gentle line.

lines.line: wedged into the fork of a branch by a songbird with better taste in treasure than in architecture.
lines.why: Funny, and it made the nest feel like part of the world, not just a prop.

lines.line: deft fingers, and not, one suspects, entirely honest ones.
lines.why: A sly hint that someone else (a thief?) is meant to open the egg, so I left it closed.

lines.line: The trap door crashes shut, and you hear someone barring it.
lines.why: A sudden sense of being trapped and watched.

lines.line: Your load is too heavy, the sword not least of it.
lines.why: A weight-limit message with some personality.

fun.why: Finding the egg and getting it home was satisfying, and the side trip through the troll and the Loud Room was fun too.

engagement.why: The hints in the descriptions kept me careful with the egg and curious about what lay underground.

difficulty.why: The egg goal itself was straightforward: climb the tree, take the egg, walk back. The troll fell in one blow. The Loud Room was the only real puzzle.

interestingness.why: The new touches, the case expecting treasures and the clasp needing dishonest fingers, made a familiar-feeling place read as its own.

prose.why: Witty, compact descriptions, though some actions just answer 'Done.'
